layoutData.body:
Pacific Coast Logistics Ltd. was founded in 1991 and incorporated in British Columbia in June 1998. Over three decades, the company has built a reputation as a reliable regional carrier and logistics provider serving customers throughout the Lower Mainland, Fraser Valley, Okanagan, and into Alberta.

The business operates four complementary service lines: dry van truckload and regional distribution, temperature-controlled refrigerated transport, third-party warehousing and cross-dock services, and Port of Vancouver container drayage. This integrated offering allows the company to serve customers across food distribution and grocery, building supply, beverage, pet food, furniture, and dairy sectors with both transportation and warehousing solutions under one roof.

In October 2022, Pacific Coast relocated to a purpose-built 110,000 square foot facility at Campbell Ridge Drive in Surrey. The move consolidated all operations under one roof and added significant warehousing capacity, including a 22,000 square foot temperature-controlled cooler. The investment positioned the company for the next phase of growth in its 3PL operations.

Pacific Coast has earned customer loyalty through demonstrated reliability during major supply chain disruptions. During the November 2021 BC floods when Highway 1 was cut at Sumas and Highway 3 through the Interior was closed, the company kept grocery stores fully stocked by finding alternative routes and running extended shifts. The same commitment to service continuity was demonstrated throughout COVID-19 and during severe winter weather events, reinforcing long-standing relationships with key customers and building the company's reputation as a carrier that delivers when it matters most.

layoutData.body:
Pacific Coast Logistics serves a diversified base of over 300 active customers across British Columbia and the Pacific Northwest. The largest customer, Alderbrook Grocery Distributors, represents 22 percent of annual revenue under a master service agreement that runs through March 2027. The company has maintained this relationship since 2009, spanning nearly two decades of consistent service.

The second-largest account contributes approximately 8 percent of revenue, and no other single customer exceeds 7 percent of total volume. The top five customers together account for 47 percent of annual revenue, while the remaining majority is distributed across nearly 300 smaller accounts, including spot freight and seasonal shippers.

The customer mix spans multiple sectors, with food-related freight representing approximately 50 percent of the business. This includes grocery distribution, produce cross-docking, beverage delivery, dairy co-op logistics, and pet food transportation. Other significant sectors include building supply, furniture, and general freight.

The company demonstrated the strength of these relationships during the November 2021 British Columbia floods, when Highway 1 was cut at Sumas and the Coquihalla Highway was closed. Pacific Coast kept Alderbrook stores fully supplied throughout the crisis by rerouting through alternative highways and extending driver hours. This performance during a critical disruption reinforced customer loyalty and showcased the operational resilience that anchor clients value.

The diversification across 300-plus accounts provides revenue stability while maintaining meaningful scale with anchor customers. Long-standing relationships, many spanning 20 to 25 years, reflect the company's reputation for reliability and its ability to retain major accounts across economic cycles and supply chain disruptions.

left.title: Services & Capabilities
left.content:
The company operates a full-service 3PL warehousing and cross-dock facility at its Surrey headquarters, offering both ambient and temperature-controlled storage alongside a complete suite of value-added services.

Storage options include ambient dry storage and a 22,000 square foot walk-in cooler with dedicated loading doors on the north side. Cross-dock and transload services handle ocean containers from the Port of Vancouver, enabling customers to deconsolidate imports and consolidate outbound shipments without long-term storage. Pick-and-pack fulfillment, pallet build, labelling and inventory reporting round out the service offering.

Operations are managed through Magaya warehouse management system with a customer portal that provides real-time inventory visibility, order status and reporting. The facility handles both dedicated storage blocks under fixed monthly agreements and transactional throughput business billed per pallet or per container.

Warehousing revenue has grown 35.5 percent from FY2022 to FY2024, reflecting strong demand for temperature-controlled storage and cross-dock capacity in the Fraser Valley. The service line generated $6,720,000 in FY2024, representing 22 percent of total company revenue and carrying higher margins than over-the-road trucking.

items.title: Establish Alberta cross-dock facility in Calgary
items.description: Open a 25,000 to 30,000 square foot cross-dock operation in Calgary to run dedicated lanes for customers shipping to Alberta. This would allow the company to offer end-to-end service on its highest-volume eastbound routes, capture backhaul opportunities, and reduce reliance on purchased transportation in the Alberta market.

items.title: Transition port and city operations to electric tractors
items.description: Two battery-electric day cab tractors are on order for delivery in mid-2026 with provincial incentive support. The lease permits installation of six Level 3 chargers in the truck court. Electric day cabs are well-suited to the predictable routes and daily return-to-base operations of port drayage and city delivery, offering lower operating costs and positioning the company ahead of future emissions regulations.

items.description: The current master service agreement with Alderbrook Grocery Distributors runs through March 31, 2027. Verbal discussions are underway regarding a three-year extension to 2030, which would provide long-term revenue visibility for the company's largest customer relationship and further strengthen the partnership built over 17 years.

items.title: Long-Standing Customer Relationships
items.description: Many customers have been with the company for 20 to 25 years. The largest customer, Alderbrook Grocery Distributors, has been a client since 2009—a 17-year relationship built on personal trust with senior decision-makers. These deep relationships provide revenue stability and reduce customer acquisition costs.

items.title: Proven Crisis Performance
items.description: During the 2021 BC floods when the Coquihalla Highway was cut at Sumas, Pacific Coast kept stores fully stocked by finding alternative routes and running extended shifts. Similar reliability was demonstrated during COVID-19 and snow events. This track record strengthened customer loyalty and cemented the company's reputation as a carrier that delivers when it matters most.

items.title: Low Driver Turnover & Tenure
items.description: Driver turnover was just 18 percent in 2024, well below industry norms. Average driver tenure is just over 6 years, with 24 drivers having over 10 years of service and the longest-tenured driver at 26.8 years. This stability reduces recruiting and training costs, improves safety, and ensures consistent service quality.

items.title: Diversified Customer Base
items.description: Over 300 active customers across food distribution, building supply, beverage, pet food, furniture, and dairy sectors. The largest customer represents 22 percent of revenue, the second-largest approximately 8 percent, and the top five together account for 47 percent. This diversification insulates the business from single-customer risk while maintaining meaningful anchor relationships.

items.title: Integrated Trucking & Warehousing
items.description: The combined offering of dry van and reefer trucking with 110,000 square feet of warehousing and cross-dock creates a competitive moat. Customers value the ability to consolidate transport and storage with one provider, and the warehousing operation generated 35.5 percent revenue growth from 2022 to 2024, driving higher overall margins.

items.title: Strong Safety Culture & Compliance
items.description: NSC Satisfactory rating, WorkSafeBC COR certification, and Partners in Protection membership since 2016. The 2024 CVSA out-of-service rate of 9.4 percent was below the national average, with only 3 reportable collisions (1 preventable, 0.11 per million kilometres) and zero fatalities. Samsara cameras in every tractor and a dedicated safety manager ensure continuous improvement.

items.description: All operating authorities transfer with the share sale: National Safety Code (BC) certificate, USDOT number, Port of Vancouver truck licensing, and Partners in Protection (CBSA) enrollment. No reapplication required.

items.description: The Barnston Road yard and shop facility is owned separately by Grewal Family Holdings Ltd. and leased to Pacific Coast Logistics on a month-to-month basis at $96,000 annually. This arrangement will continue post-sale or be renegotiated at fair market rent (estimated at $14,500 per month based on comparable properties).

layoutData.body:
Pacific Coast Logistics represents an ideal acquisition opportunity for a growth-minded buyer seeking to establish or expand a regional platform in Western Canada. The seller envisions a buyer with the operational scale and capital resources to build on the company's strengths — a larger carrier looking to add regional density and warehousing capabilities, or a private-equity-backed platform assembling a multi-site operation across British Columbia and Alberta.

The business has been carefully positioned for integration into a larger enterprise. The 110,000-square-foot warehouse facility includes landlord pre-approval for up to 15,000 square feet of additional cooler expansion, offering immediate growth capacity. The fleet is well-maintained with an average age of approximately three years, minimizing near-term capital requirements. Established relationships with over 300 customers — including a 17-year partnership with the largest grocery distributor account — provide a stable revenue foundation, while the company's demonstrated ability to retain drivers (average tenure just over six years, 18 percent annual turnover) addresses one of the industry's most persistent challenges.

Manpreet Grewal, the current VP Operations and a 25 percent owner, has committed to staying for a minimum of two to three years post-sale as General Manager or VP Operations, ensuring continuity in customer relationships, dispatch operations, warehouse management, and shop oversight. The seller is also open to rolling 10 to 15 percent of proceeds into the buyer's entity if the right strategic partner emerges.

This opportunity is not suited to a national carrier seeking to convert the operation into a line-haul terminal and eliminate the warehousing side of the business. The warehouse operation has grown 35 percent from 2022 to 2024 and operates at 88 percent capacity, generating higher margins than trucking alone. The combined trucking and warehousing model is a key competitive advantage, particularly with grocery and food distribution customers who value single-source supply chain solutions.

The ideal buyer will recognize the value in preserving and expanding the integrated logistics model, leveraging Pacific Coast's reputation for reliability — proven during the 2021 BC floods when the company kept stores supplied despite highway closures — and using the Surrey facility as a hub for further growth across the Lower Mainland, the Okanagan, and into Alberta.

layoutData.body:
Harjit Singh Grewal, the founder and President of Pacific Coast Logistics, is selling the business after 34 years in trucking to transition into retirement. The yard property at Barnston Road will remain with the family as a long-term asset and pension, leased back to the buyer on terms to be negotiated at close.

Manpreet Grewal, the Vice-President of Operations and 25 percent shareholder, will remain with the company for a minimum of two to three years post-sale in the capacity of General Manager or VP Operations. Manpreet has run dispatch, warehouse operations, shop oversight, and safety for over a decade and holds the key operational relationships. For the right buyer—a larger carrier or private-equity-backed platform building out Western Canada—Manpreet is open to rolling 10 to 15 percent of proceeds into the buyer's entity as equity, aligning long-term interests and ensuring continuity.

Harjit will provide six to twelve months of transition support focused on customer relationship handoff and introductions. The President knows many of the key customers personally, some for 20 to 25 years, and those relationships—particularly with Alderbrook's VP of Logistics Doug Fairweather—will require intentional transition beyond the contract assignments. The Alderbrook relationship, which represents 22 percent of revenue and has run for 17 years, is held personally by Harjit; the buyer should plan for joint calls, facility visits, and a gradual handoff supported by Manpreet's existing operational rapport.

The management team beyond the owners is stable, experienced, and prepared to continue under new ownership. The controller, dispatch manager, warehouse manager, safety manager, and shop foreman have an average tenure of over ten years and are committed to the business. The shop foreman, Dale, plans to retire in 2027, but a successor has already been identified and is being trained.

This is a structured, low-risk transition with multi-year operational continuity, direct owner involvement during handoff, and the option for meaningful equity partnership with the next-generation operator already running the business day to day.
